title: A section of an invertible module trivializes it where it does not vanish
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme, $\mathcal L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] and $s\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal L)$. Put $Y_s=\{y\in Y:\ s_y\notin\mathfrak m_y\mathcal L_y\}$ (equivalently, the set of $y$ where the value $s(y)$ of $s$ in $\mathcal L_y\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y,y}}\kappa(y)$ is nonzero; $\kappa(y)$ the residue field [def-weil-residue-field]). Then $Y_s$ is open in $Y$, and the map $\mathcal O_{Y_s}\to\mathcal L|_{Y_s}$, $a\mapsto a\,s|$, is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{Y_s}$-modules. Consequently, for every open $V\subseteq Y_s$ and every $t\in\mathcal L(V)$ there is a unique $a\in\mathcal O_Y(V)$ with $t=a\cdot s|_V$; it is written $t/s$.

proof.text: *The value $s(y)$.* For $y\in Y$, $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ is a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_y$ and $\kappa(y)=\mathcal O_{Y,y}/\mathfrak m_y$ [def-weil-residue-field]; for any $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$-module $M$, $M\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y,y}}\kappa(y)=M/\mathfrak m_yM$ ($M\otimes_AA/\mathfrak m=M/\mathfrak mM$), and under this identification $s(y)=s_y\otimes1$ is the class of $s_y$. So $s(y)\neq0$ iff $s_y\notin\mathfrak m_y\mathcal L_y$: the two descriptions of $Y_s$ in the statement agree.

proof.text: *Local trivialization and the stalks.* Since $\mathcal L$ is invertible [def-sc-invertible-module], every $y_0\in Y$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ with an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_U$-modules $\varphi:\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal L|_U$. Put $e=\varphi_U(1)\in\mathcal L(U)$ and $g=\varphi_U^{-1}(s|_U)\in\mathcal O_Y(U)$; since $\varphi$ is $\mathcal O$-linear, $\varphi_V(a)=a\,e|_V$ for every open $V\subseteq U$ and $a\in\mathcal O_Y(V)$, and $s|_U=g\,e$. For $y\in U$, taking stalks gives an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$-modules $\varphi_y:\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to\mathcal L_y$, $a\mapsto a\,e_y$ (stalks of $\mathcal O_U$, $\mathcal L|_U$ at $y$ are those of $\mathcal O_Y$, $\mathcal L$, the open neighbourhoods of $y$ inside $U$ being cofinal). Hence $\mathcal L_y$ is free of rank one with basis $e_y$, in particular finitely generated, and $s_y=g_y\,e_y$. An isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$-modules carries $\mathfrak m_y\mathcal O_{Y,y}=\mathfrak m_y$ onto $\mathfrak m_y\mathcal L_y$, so $s_y\in\mathfrak m_y\mathcal L_y$ iff $g_y\in\mathfrak m_y$. With $D(g)=\{y\in U: g_y\notin\mathfrak m_y\}$ [lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-function] this gives $Y_s\cap U=D(g)$; equivalently (by that lemma, (a)) $Y_s\cap U=\{y\in U: g(y)\neq0\text{ in }\kappa(y)\}$.

source.place: Properties, Lemma Tag 01PW (lemma-invert-s-sections), first paragraph of the proof: with $\mathcal L|_{U_j}\cong\mathcal O_{U_j}$, $s|_{U_j}$ corresponds to $f_j$ and $X_s\cap U_j=D(f_j)$ (stated there without argument; the argument written out here)

proof.text: *$Y_s$ is open.* By step 2 the opens $U$ on which $\mathcal L$ is trivial cover $Y$, and for each of them $Y_s\cap U=D(g)$ is open in $Y$ [lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-function, (b)]. Hence $Y_s=\bigcup_U(Y_s\cap U)$ is open in $Y$. (Stacks proves openness by producing the section $t$ of $\mathcal L^{\otimes-1}$ near $x$; on a trivializing $U$ this is the same argument, $t$ corresponding to $g^{-1}$ on $D(g)$.)

proof.text: *The map $\mu$.* Regard $Y_s$ as an open subscheme, with $\mathcal O_{Y_s}=\mathcal O_Y|_{Y_s}$. For an open $V\subseteq Y_s$ let $\mu_V:\mathcal O_Y(V)\to\mathcal L(V)$, $a\mapsto a\,s|_V$. Each $\mu_V$ is $\mathcal O_Y(V)$-linear, and for $W\subseteq V$ one has $(a\,s|_V)|_W=a|_W\,s|_W$ (restriction in an $\mathcal O_Y$-module is compatible with the module structure), so $\mu$ is a morphism of $\mathcal O_{Y_s}$-modules $\mathcal O_{Y_s}\to\mathcal L|_{Y_s}$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Modules, Lemma Tag 01CY (lemma-s-open), statement: 'the map $s:\mathcal O_{X_s}\to\mathcal L|_{X_s}$'

proof.text: *$\mu$ is bijective on stalks.* Let $y\in Y_s$. The stalk of $\mathcal O_{Y_s}$ (resp. $\mathcal L|_{Y_s}$) at $y$ is $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ (resp. $\mathcal L_y$), the open neighbourhoods of $y$ inside the open $Y_s$ being cofinal, and $\mu_y(a)=a\,s_y$ (the germ of $a\,s|_V$ is $a_y s_y$). By step 2, $\mathcal L_y$ is a free $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$-module of rank one with a basis $e_y$, so $\mathcal L_y/\mathfrak m_y\mathcal L_y\cong\kappa(y)$ is one-dimensional over $\kappa(y)$ [def-weil-residue-field]; as $y\in Y_s$, the class of $s_y$ in it is nonzero, hence spans it. By Nakayama [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] (local ring $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, finitely generated module $\mathcal L_y$, one element $s_y$), $s_y$ generates $\mathcal L_y$: $\mu_y$ is surjective. Injectivity: write $s_y=u\,e_y$ with $u\in\mathcal O_{Y,y}$; surjectivity gives $b$ with $b\,s_y=e_y$, i.e. $(bu-1)e_y=0$, so $bu=1$ because $e_y$ is a basis; if $a\,s_y=0$ then $au\,e_y=0$, so $au=0$ and $a=aub=0$. Thus $\mu_y$ is bijective, i.e. $s_y$ is a basis of $\mathcal L_y$.

proof.text: *$\mu$ is an isomorphism.* $\mu$ is a morphism of $\mathcal O_{Y_s}$-modules on the scheme $Y_s$ (step 4) whose stalk maps at all points of $Y_s$ are bijective (step 5); by [lem-weil-pbc-module-iso-on-stalks] it is an isomorphism $\mathcal O_{Y_s}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L|_{Y_s}$.

split_report.summary: Split in seven steps following Stacks 01CY: (1) the two descriptions of Y_s agree (M⊗κ = M/𝔪M); (2) on a trivializing open U, s = g·e and Y_s∩U = D(g), stalks L_y free of rank one; (3) Y_s open via the new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-function (Scheme.basicOpen, mem_basicOpen, evaluation_ne_zero_iff_mem_basicOpen, isUnit_res_basicOpen; Stacks Schemes 01HZ); (4) μ: a ↦ a·s is O-linear; (5) μ_y bijective at y∈Y_s by Nakayama (lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators) plus a written-out injectivity argument; (6) μ an isomorphism by lem-weil-pbc-module-iso-on-stalks; (7) the unique quotient t/s. Openness uses the local trivialization (as in the proof of Properties 01PW) rather than Stacks' section of L^{⊗-1}, so no dual/tensor nodes are needed; the statement does not claim the section s' of L^{⊗-1} and is unchanged. def-pc-scheme added to stmt_deps.
